text: ! command — step one of Rex as the harness. Type !cmd in the web box: Rex runs it in a new visible tab on the pane's computer, in the agent's folder, then hands the output to Claude Code / Codex / Pi. Three ways it can read in the thread:

A · Inline run
Wins when: ! is a convenience and the agent stays the star; no new vocabulary.
Cost: Rex is invisible — looks like the agent ran it. Doesn't build toward Rex as the harness.

B · Tab-first
Wins when: commands are mostly interactive (logins, prompts) and the Rex tab is the place you want to be.
Cost: context switch every time; the thread only gets a receipt.

C · Rex speaks (recommended)
Wins when: Rex is meant to become the harness — Rex gets its own mark and voice in the thread, answers prompts inline, and the hand-off to the agent is explicit. Scales to future Rex-owned features (routing between agents, Rex memory, /rex commands).
Cost: a third participant to define and keep consistent.
